sourceLocators: Vasilevsky, Delo vsei zhizni, chapter 16, 249–251, reproducing the December 13 directive; Ziemke and Bauer, Moscow to Stalingrad, 485–486, on the differing retrospective chronologies.https://militera.lib.ru/memo/russian/vasilevsky/16.html

Ziemke and Bauer, Moscow to Stalingrad, 486–487; Scianna, Italian War, 158–169.

states.label: Tatsinskaya: the airlift base disrupted
states.title: Tatsinskaya: the airlift base disrupted
states.description: 24th Tank Corps reaches Tatsinskaya. The loss and dispersal of ground facilities disrupt air supply even where aircraft escape.
sourceLocators: Vasilevsky, Delo vsei zhizni, chapter 16, 260–261, on Badanov's corps, the December 24 attack, isolation, and breakout. His favourable characterization of the return is retained as a claim rather than a casualty accounting.

Ziemke and Bauer, Moscow to Stalingrad, 489–490; Morzik, Airlift Operations, 190–191, on base relocation and support losses.

states.label: Iskra opens a land corridor
states.title: Iskra opens a land corridor
states.description: Soviet forces join south of Ladoga and recover Shlisselburg. A narrow corridor opens; the siege continues and the new railway is not yet operating.
sourceLocators: Boris Yeltsin Presidential Library, “Unikalnye arkhivnye dokumenty,” description of the January 18 meeting act; Artillery Museum, “Operatsiya ‘Iskra’,” account of the junctions. The meeting act is known here through the library's published description, not an examination of its original sheet.https://www.prlib.ru/news/1938234

Krivosheev, Stamp of Secrecy Is Removed, English translation, 163–164 (PDF pages 172–173), “The Operation to Break the Blockade of Leningrad.”https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/SovietLosses.pdf
